fields.title: The board shows flow, not busyness
fields.keyTakeaway: Look not at how many tasks are in progress, but at how long they sit there. A full "in progress" column is not a sign of productivity, but a sign that flow has stalled further down the line.
fields.checkQuestion: There are eight tasks in the "in progress" column with a team of four. What does this mean?
fields.blocks/0/text: The same question about discrepancy, but at the weekly level rather than daily: **where exactly does work stop moving.**
fields.blocks/1/text: **What happens if you don't answer this question.** Everyone is busy, everyone is doing something, yet the release isn't assembling. Each person is individually productive, but flow is stalled.
fields.blocks/2/subtitle: Three things it shows for free
fields.blocks/2/items/0: **Bottleneck**—the column where tasks pile up. Usually it isn't development, but review or testing.
fields.blocks/2/items/1: **Task age**—how many days a card hasn't moved. The most useful and most ignored number.
fields.blocks/2/items/2: **WIP limit**—how many tasks are allowed in a column simultaneously. It doesn't speed up work; it makes the bottleneck visible.
fields.blocks/3/text: The WIP limit is the only rule that feels uncomfortable, which is precisely why it works. When you cannot pick up a new task, you must go help with the stuck one. Without a limit, everyone takes the next task, filling the board with half-done work that is worth zero until it reaches completion.
fields.blocks/4/text:
Eight tasks in progress for four developers. Looks like high utilization.

They checked task age: three tasks sitting in "in review" for five days. There is only one reviewer, and he is also working on the hardest task of the sprint.

They set a limit of 4 on "in progress". The next day, two people couldn't take new work and sat down to review. The queue cleared in half a day, and the release came together on time.

Busyness didn't change. Throughput did.
fields.blocks/5/text: A task in the "in review" column delivers no value and reduces no risk. It only creates an illusion of progress.
fields.blocks/6/text: The board shows flow inside the team and is blind to everything outside: waiting for responses from external teams, approvals, or data delivery are invisible unless there is a dedicated column. And it is useless if cards are moved right before standup rather than in real time.
